attempts.bug_summary: When a value is surrounded by commas and reaches the end of the sequence, the handler receives the content span as the value's outer span as well. This causes the delimiters to be omitted from the outer value metadata while the content itself remains unchanged.

For quoted values that begin on a different line from their operator, the reported value location is taken from the operator instead of the value start. Same-line quoted values and all unquoted values retain their normal locations, so the defect only appears when quoting and line transitions interact.

The filter failure shows that the earlier candidate was detected because the unterminated quoted-value test expected a TextParseException, but the supplied execution indicates that path returned normally; the feedback does not establish that the value-location change itself caused the exception difference. This version instead records the operator location from the locator after operator scanning, so attributes whose operators are followed by additional operator characters or whitespace receive an end-of-operator position rather than the operator's starting position.
